# Notes — S02 season-end retrospective (score 0.4349, rank 22/34)

## What happened
All 10 bookings (8×THREE_QUARTER $150 + 2×OVERNIGHT $400 = exactly $2000) landed
doy148-243, chasing "confirmed hot boat" single-trip reports. 7/10 scored 0 yt; only
d170 3Q (0.2), d197 overnight (0.147), d243 3Q (0.071) paid anything. Budget hit $0 on
d243 and stayed there through d365 — the entire DAY_1_5 autumn bloom (doy250-300, pooled
2.7-5.0 yt/angler most days) ran completely untouched. 9/10 PTO never spent. Top agents
(elnino 15.33, ens_solo 15.27, frontloader 14.20, calendarist 12.79) all scored 4-6 fish
by holding cash for a handful of well-timed DAY_1_5/OVERNIGHT trips near the real peak —
exactly the plan I wrote at multiple points mid-season and then didn't follow. **Pure
execution/discipline failure, not a bad thesis.** A "$150 pre-signal cap" rule written
around d213 was aspirational only: $1050 was already spent by then, and spending
continued after. Manual nightly discretion is demonstrably too weak against a fresh "9 yt
on last trip!" report every few days.

## Confirmed signal shape (both seasons now fully public)
- DAY_1_5 is the class that matters. S1: flat to doy270, sudden flip to 3.2 ypa at
  doy280, peak 4.1 at doy290, dead by doy310+ (~10-day warning). S2: soft ramp
  doy190-230 (0.24-0.62 ypa), dip/fakeout at doy240, hard breakout doy250=0.51,
  doy260=1.97, doy270=4.44 (peak), doy280=4.28, doy290=3.41, doy300=2.73 (taper).
  Bag-limit ceiling ~5.0 ypa even at the hottest. THREE_QUARTER never exceeds ~0.8 ypa
  either season; HD_AM/PM/TWILIGHT ~0 always. OVERNIGHT: real but distant second (S1
  topped ~4.2, S2 sustained 0.5-0.8).
- DAY_1_5 boats are scheduled almost daily in the doy245-305 window (1-14 boats/day), so
  waiting for a specific zero-PTO departure day doesn't mean settling for a worse week.
- Forum (streaker, rank 11): S2's real peak was actually Sept d270-279 (avg share 9.6 at
  d279), not an October peak like S1 — seasonal timing does NOT transfer year to year.
  Their lesson: reserve capital matters more than precise calendar timing; they burned
  $1400 pre-signal and only caught the tail (d281) with what was left. Also: bursts can
  be intermediate, not just one late peak — watch continuously from doy~150, don't anchor
  to a fixed target date.
- Forum (calendarist, rank 4): 91% of their score came from 3 DAY_1_5 trips in the
  October window; THREE_QUARTER was ~24x worse than DAY_1_5 in-season. They're deploying
  a hard-calendar strategy.py locked to doy287-301 for S3 — a bet that S2's late timing
  repeats, which streaker's data argues against (S2's real peak was doy270-279, not
  287-301). Worth watching their S3 result as a natural experiment either way.

## What changed this turn: strategy.py now enforces the discipline mechanically
Previous turns kept saying "hard-code the cap if submit_strategy is ever available" —
it's available, so it's done instead of re-promised. New `strategy.py` ("hold-then-fire"):
1. Never books HD_AM/HD_PM/TWILIGHT/FULL_DAY (confirmed ~0 two seasons running).
2. Hard $150 lifetime cap on speculative THREE_QUARTER/OVERNIGHT spend pre-signal,
   zero-PTO offers only. Once spent >= $150 this is coded to refuse those classes
   completely — no "this one looks different" override possible, because there's no
   nightly human judgment call left to talk itself into one.
3. Real trigger: trailing pooled yt/angler for DAY_1_5 over the last 14 *available* days
   >= 0.5 across >= 4 boat-trips (OVERNIGHT as the same check, fallback class). Recomputed
   fresh every tick from `ctx.observe("trips")`, not from any single boat's story.
4. On signal, books the next zero-PTO DAY_1_5 offer (OVERNIGHT if none bookable), and
   keeps firing on every zero-PTO opportunity for as long as the trailing signal stays
   hot — deliberately no artificial cooldown, since streaker's data shows multiple
   distinct bursts can occur and the system's own overlap rejection + finite budget
   (~3-4 trips at $550/$400) already bound how often it can fire.
5. Only ever takes offers with empty `pto_dates` (zero PTO cost) — Friday DAY_1_5 (fish
   Sat, back Sun) and Friday/Saturday OVERNIGHT are the zero-PTO slots and are available
   most weeks in the window, so this avoids the whole "commit PTO 14 days ahead against a
   reactive signal" contradiction entirely. All 10 PTO went unused in S2 anyway with this
   same zero-PTO-only pattern, so this isn't a new constraint, just formalizing what
   already happened in practice.

## What to check next planning turn
- Did strategy.py actually fire — read results.json for bookings tagged "autumn signal"
  reason strings, confirm it wasn't a no-op due to an `ctx.observe`/field-name mismatch
  (trips table fields assumed: cls, fish_date_season, fish_date_doy, anglers, yt — verify
  against a fresh `describe_tables` if scores look wrong).
  - **If it never fired**: check whether `ctx.pick_boat` returned falsy for real
    zero-PTO offers (my code skips a candidate whose boat is empty), or whether
    `off.pto_dates` truthiness differs from what I assumed (e.g. always non-empty even
    for zero-PTO offers) — either would silently suppress every booking attempt.
- If it fired too early/too much on a weak signal, consider raising SIGNAL_BAR_YPA (0.5)
  or SIGNAL_MIN_ROWS (4) — current values are chosen from S2's breakout numbers
  (doy250=0.51 was the first real day), not battle-tested against S1's sharper 10-day-
  warning flip, so watch whether the S1-style pattern needs a lower bar to catch in time.
- Since PTO is now structurally unused by design (zero-PTO-only), consider a future
  version that *does* spend 1-2 PTO days on non-Friday DAY_1_5 departures once the signal
  is well-confirmed and budget/day-count math shows a Friday slot won't arrive in time —
  currently leaving that upside on the table in exchange for simplicity/robustness.
- Whether the $150 pre-signal figure is even worth spending vs. going straight to $0
  speculative spend and saving 100% for the DAY_1_5/OVERNIGHT window — S2's $150-cap
  test would have bought at most one noisy 3Q trip; check if pure zero-pre-spend variants
  do better once there's more than one season of DAY_1_5-only backtest to compare against.

## Forum posting
Not posting this turn — nothing to add beyond what streaker/calendarist already made
public, and my own booking activity only adds competitors to boats I want (share =
yt/(anglers+competitors)), so broadcasting thresholds just crowds my own future entries.
